title: ‘Davidson Window’ Admiral Hopes He Was Wrong On China’s Ability To Take Taiwan By 2027
zh_title: “戴维森之窗”海军上将希望他对中国 2027 年占领台湾能力的判断是错误的
summary: 五年前，这位在国会作证的人提出了所谓的“戴维森窗口”，即中国有能力在 2027 年之前对台湾发动可信的入侵，现在这个日期即将到来，他为他的想法提供了一些见解。当时在太平洋地区指挥美军的海军上将菲利普·戴维森 (Philip Davidson) 在周五发布的播客中表示，自他 2021 年退役以来发生的一些事态发展可能会改变他的预测。然而，美国印太司令部（现太平洋司令部或PACOM）前司令告诉我们为什么要关心这个问题
content:
五年前，这位在国会作证的人提出了所谓的“戴维森窗口”，即中国有能力在 2027 年之前对台湾发动可信的入侵，现在这个日期即将到来，他为他的想法提供了一些见解。当时在太平洋地区指挥美军的海军上将菲利普·戴维森 (Philip Davidson) 在周五发布的播客中表示，自他 2021 年退役以来发生的一些事态发展可能会改变他的预测。然而，美国印太司令部（现太平洋司令部或PACOM）前司令告诉《我们为什么要关心印太？》他仍然认为有理由担心。他特别敦促美国在入侵台湾之前向台湾提供军事援助，以更好地威慑中国采取行动。中国军队练习海滩登陆。 (解放军) 戴维森发表上述声明之际，中国一直在稳步增加在台湾周边的军事演习，中国认为台湾是一个分裂的省份，有朝一日将重新置于其控制之下。在了解戴维森对 SeaLight 基金会创始人兼执行董事雷·鲍威尔 (Ray Powell) 和 BowerGroupAsia 高级顾问吉姆·卡鲁索 (Jim Carouso) 所说的话之前，让我们回顾一下戴维森于 2021 年 3 月 9 日对参议院军事委员会所说的话。
戴维森在谈到中国​​时表示：“我担心他们正在加速实现取代美国的野心，以及我们在基于规则的国际秩序中发挥领导作用的野心，他们长期以来一直表示希望在 2050 年之前实现这一目标，我担心他们会进一步接近这一目标。”菲利普·戴维森，当时担任海军上将和美国印度太平洋司令部司令。 （美国海军）两年后，对所谓“戴维森之窗”的评估得到了中央情报局（CIA）的支持。时任中央情报局局长比尔·伯恩斯 (Bill Burns) 表示：“习主席已指示中国军事领导层解放军 (PLA) 在 2027 年之前做好入侵台湾的准备。”从那以后发生了什么变化？ “从本质上讲，我希望我是错的，”戴维森在谈到他的国会证词时说道。 “如果我错了，那就意味着我们向印太司令部建议的事情、美国政府和其他国家政府在过去七年里采取的事情是有效的。而且没有发生战争。” “我主张，从军事意义上来说，五套能力——我认为很重要的投资指南，”戴维森解释道，他现在是国防承包商 AV 的董事会成员。
“美国需要重新考虑其在印太地区的兵力态势和设计——我们在哪里、我们如何部署、我们轮换什么、这些部队的能力是什么。我们还需要更多样化、更大规模的联合部队火力，这意味着进攻性火力不仅来自海上，还来自陆地和空中。”这位海军上将补充道：“你现在肯定会看到这种情况正在发生，包括部署和导弹部署、海军陆战队、陆军在菲律宾和第一岛链沿线的部署。” “这很有帮助。”第 1 多域特遣部队远程火力营第 3 野战炮兵团第 5 营查理炮台的中程能力 (MRC) 发射器抵达菲律宾吕宋岛北部战区，这是该能力首次部署到战区的一部分

【原文 English Original】
The man whose congressional testimony five years ago led to what’s known as the “Davidson Window” for China being capable of launching a credible invasion of Taiwan by 2027 is offering some insights into what he is thinking now that the date is drawing near. Philip Davidson – the admiral who led U.S. forces in the Pacific at the time – said on a podcast released Friday that several developments have taken place since he retired in 2021 that could change his projection. However, the former commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (now Pacific Command or PACOM) told the Why Should We Care About the Indo-Pacific? podcast he still sees reasons for concern. In particular, he urged the U.S. to deliver military aid to Taiwan before an invasion to better deter China from acting. Chinese forces practice a beach landing. (PLA) Davidson’s statements were delivered as China has been steadily increasing military exercises around Taiwan , which it considers a breakaway province that it will someday bring back under its control. Before getting into what Davidson told podcasters Ray Powell, founder and executive director of the SeaLight Foundation , and Jim Carouso, a senior advisor at BowerGroupAsia , let’s recall what Davidson told the Senate Armed Services Committee on March 9, 2021. “I worry that they are accelerating their ambitions to supplant the United States, and our leadership role in the rules-based international order, which they have long said that they want to do that by 2050, I am worried about them moving that target closer,” Davidson said of China. “Taiwan is clearly one of their ambitions before then, and I think the threat is manifest during this decade, in fact, in the next six years.” Philip Davidson when he was a Navy admiral and commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command. (USN) The assessment of the so-called “Davidson Window” was backed two years later by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). “President Xi has instructed the PLA [People’s Liberation Army], the Chinese military leadership, to be ready by 2027 to invade Taiwan,” then-CIA Director Bill Burns stated . What’s Changed Since Then? “At the heart of it, I’m hoping to be wrong,” said Davidson about his congressional testimony. “If I’m wrong, that means the things we recommended from Indo-Pacific Command, the things that the United States government and other governments have undertaken over the last seven years, have been effective. And there hasn’t been war.” “I advocated for, just in the military sense, five capability sets – investment guidelines that I thought were important to do,” explained Davidson, now on the board of directors at defense contractor AV . “The United States needed to rethink its force posture and design in the region, in the Indo-Pacific – where we are, how we deployed, what we rotated through, what the capabilities of those sets were. We also needed more diverse and a larger set of joint force fires, meaning offensive fires, not just from the sea, but from land and air domain.” “You’re certainly seeing that play out right now, with deployments and missile deployments, with Marine formations , Army formations in the Philippines and along the First Island Chain,” the admiral added. “That has been a help.” Mid-Range Capability (MRC) Launcher from Charlie Battery, 5th Battalion, 3rd Field Artillery Regiment, Long Range Fires Battalion, 1st Multi-Domain Task Force arrives as part of the capability’s first deployment into theater on Northern Luzon, Philippines, April 8, 2024. The MRC deployment aims to enhance Philippine maritime defense capabilities, while bolstering interoperability and readiness within the U.S.-Philippine Alliance. (U.S. Army) U.S. Army In addition, Davidson noted that the U.S. “needed to improve our exercises, our experimentation, and our innovation in the region. We have deepened the relationship with Japan and Australia in the Keen series of exercises over the last five years, and in a way that was kind of unheard of in my day, which I think is a profound improvement.” The Keen Sword training exercise occurred last month and saw about “45,000 Japan Self-Defense Force, 11,000 U.S. service members and forces from Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines…participating alongside observers from the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom,” according to the U.S. Navy. A Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Landing Craft Air Cushion (LCAC) hovercraft assigned to Amphibious Warfare Squadron One, Amphibious and Mine Warfare Group, coasts into the harbor at Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni, Japan, Oct. 28, 2026, during Keen Sword. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Donald Dugger) Lance Cpl. Donald Dugger Japan taking a more assertive security posture toward China has been a huge change from when he was in command, Davidson noted. “Japan absolutely has come forward, they reissued their national security strategy in December of [2022], and there were a number of alliance announcements made in January of [2023],” he explained.  The Japanese doubled their investment in defense from 1% to 2% of its GDP, Davidson highlighted. Japan also “established space [and] cyber forces, instilled the cybersecurity principles and laws that would be necessary to deepen our relationship in a classified way. And this is almost unknown to anybody in America. Completely redistributed and reset their ground formations and air formations in the Southwest Island chain, between Okinawa and along the Ryukyu chain.” “Most importantly, they identified China as the strategic threat in the region,” Davidson proffered. “And in the alliance announcement in January of [2023] with us, said that our interests have converged in this regard.” A Japan Air Self-Defense Force F-15 fighter performs during the Komatsu Air Festival on September 26, 2026 in Komatsu, Japan. (Photo by Zhang Hui/VCG via Getty Images) VCG Taiwan too has made some needed improvements in its approach to defending itself since he retired, Davidson explained. “You have to be encouraged by Taiwan’s actions taken since then,” he stated. “They expanded the conscription timeline from just a few months to a year of service. They have done an enormous amount of work in their national emergency preparedness realm.” Davidson also credited Adm. Lee Hsi-min, chief of the Taiwanese Armed Forces general staff from 2017 to 2019, for developing the Overall Defense Concept (ODC). Lee envisioned a mix of mines, uncrewed aerial systems (UAS), uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs), uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs), crewed coastal defense boats, land-based mobile short- and medium-range precision munitions, precision-guided multiple launch rocket systems, man portable air defense systems (MANPADS), anti-armor rocket systems and electronic warfare measures to counter the PLA’s overwhelming advantages in aviation and naval assets and long-range fires. Taiwan sits about 130 miles east of China. (Google Earth) “He said, ‘We really have to develop the kind of asymmetric capabilities that help round out our lack of capacity vis-a-vis its relationship with the People’s Republic of China, and make sure that we have a strategic and operational design that can kill in the littoral and along the landing beaches and things like that,’” Davidson pointed out. “They’ve been getting after autonomy. They’ve been getting after robotics and drones and sensing.” In 2025, Taiwan revealed a new drone boat, or uncrewed surface vessel (USV), the Endeavor Manta, said to be the first of its kind for the Republic of China Navy (ROCN). However, as we have frequently pointed out , Taiwan is still far behind where it needs to be in many of these areas, but especially uncrewed systems . In addition, Davidson said growing relations with the Philippines and Australia are also helping. Australia signed the Australia–United Kingdom–United States security partnership (AUKUS) in September 2021, months after Davidson retired. AUKUS calls for the United States and Britain to share nuclear-submarine technology with Australia. A rendering of the future SSN-AUKUS design. (U.K. Ministry of Defense) “So over the span of the last six years since March 9 of 2021, you’ve seen a lot of change that I think has reinforced the deterrence of the West here, and I think that’s important to note,” Davidson stated. What Still Needs To Change Despite seeing the U.S. and its allies better prepared to defend against a Chinese invasion of Taiwan, Davidson said he is concerned that the U.S. is not moving fast enough to provide promised military aid. “I would like to see the $14 billion in committed [Foreign Military Sales] to Taiwan move over there in the next few months or a year,” Davidson stated. Approval of the package, which is a major point of controversy with China, has been stalled, Taiwan’s Defense Minister Wellington Koo said in September . The minister’s remarks “come as concerns mount that President Donald Trump could halt arms sales to Taiwan. China has pressed Washington to halt the arms sales, most prominently during a May summit in Beijing between Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping,” The Associated Press noted . “The United States paused the $14 billion arms deal after that meeting.” The package “largely consists of [Patriot] PAC-3 and NASAMS [ National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System ] air defense missiles,” Reuters reported . However, another huge factor beyond tensions with China is the U.S. supply of these air defense munitions, which has been drastically affected by the current and recent Middle East conflicts . Donations to Ukraine have also eaten into U.S. stocks. The lack of sufficient magazine depth is an issue that TWZ has raised frequently for years, and especially in regard to America’s air and missile defenses , in particular. Commitments for deliveries to 20 other nations and an overall insatiable global demand for interceptors due to numerous destabilizing events has put further strain on the supply of American interceptors. All this is also straining the ability of industry to provide enough capacity. For instance, current PAC-3 MSE production “is around the baseline rate of 650 interceptors per year, with half the deliveries going to the United States and the rest to allies and partners,” according to a report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). The Pentagon is trying to boost production. Under a contract with the Pentagon inked in January , Lockheed Martin is committed to raising annual Patriot output to 2,000 interceptors. A Patriot PAC-3 interceptor (Lockheed Martin) In addition to wanting to see the arms package pushed forward, Davidson warned about China’s information warfare capabilities. “The one thing that has really jumped out at me that was a problem, certainly, when I was the Indo-Pacific commander, but it’s worse now, is the information environment,” Davidson posited. “China is working to undermine the democratic processes in Taiwan. They’re working to undermine any U.S. citizens’ confidence in business leadership and political leadership and military leadership. They’re exploiting accidents or difficulties that someone might be having to flood social networks, and it’s happening not just from China, but from Russia and Iran and independent actors elsewhere. “ “It’s really dangerous,” the former commander emphasized. “There’s been some estimations that some of the activity from bots and from propaganda players is accounting for up to 70% of the commentary in social media threads here and there, and that’s a much more difficult place to be.” Davidson said the U.S. needs to step up its own information warfare capabilities. “I think we should be putting as much effort into [the information domain] as we’ve been putting into drones and autonomy and things like that in this day and age,” Davidson stated. Chinese hovercraft land on a beach during training. (PLAN) Davidson did not address some other glaring issues in regard to China’s potential seizure of Taiwan. The biggest being will the U.S. actually respond militarily if a major Chinese exercise suddenly became an actual invasion operation? Would there even be enough time and what about China’s anti-access capabilities that could keep much of America’s combat power at bay during the early stages of such a conflict? Would there even be support for such an intervention operation domestically, especially considering it could be very bloody and it would surely manifest itself here at home? Then, as we mentioned in the piece, there are many areas where Taiwan seems to be moving far too slowly while China’s military force continues to balloon on nearly all fronts. Regardless, it’s nice to hear from the man who inadvertently gave birth to the “Davidson Window” now that this ominous window of vulnerability he predicted a half decade is cracking open. Contact the author: howard@twz.com The post ‘Davidson Window’ Admiral Hopes He Was Wrong On China’s Ability To Take Taiwan By 2027 appeared first on TWZ .

zh_title: 首次出现严重受损的康涅狄格号潜艇的新弓声纳罩（更新）
summary: TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 达成了
content:
TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 联系我们，要求在进行额外审查时删除圆顶的图像。出于礼貌，我们同意了，如果完全获得批准，我们将重新发布它。 Janicki Industries 今天告诉我们，该公司在大约 10 个月内生产出了新型船首声纳导流罩，并于 2024 年交付给海军。据其网站称，Janicki 拥有为美国核潜艇项目生产“声纳罩和精密加工硬件”的历史。它还支持各种备受瞩目的航空航天项目，包括 B-21 袭击者轰炸机和 F-35 联合攻击战斗机。根据一份经过大量编辑的海军事故报告，康涅狄格号的船头在五年前的碰撞事件发生后，最初至少在某种程度上仍然保持着连接状态。然而，当潜艇一瘸一拐地驶向关岛时，整个船首结构随后断裂。
随后，这艘船驶往加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥，然后前往华盛顿州的普吉特海湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施 (PSNS-IMF)，此后一直待在那里。 2023 年，在普吉特湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施中看到的康涅狄格号航空母舰，其船首圆顶明显缺失。美国海军“普吉特海湾海军造船厂和国际货币基金组织（中间维护设施）需要按照船的计划，在其后面没有生产线的情况下安装一个精密的替换圆顶，”贾尼基在撰写本文时还在其网站上表示。 “Janicki 比次佳选择快了 24 个月，因为工作所需的一切都集中在一个屋檐下：适合半球的 5 轴铣床、证明这一点的计量方法以及形成双曲板的 1,000 吨压力机。”本文顶部的部分图片和下面的完整图片显示了 Janicki 专有的五轴铣床在圆顶上工作的情况。海狼级潜艇艏声纳导流罩的尺寸和复杂性怎么强调都不为过。这些船上的船首声纳阵列直径为 24 英尺。圆顶本身的结构必须按照非常严格的规格建造，以使声纳系统正常工作。海狼级潜艇上的艏声纳阵列，其艏穹顶被拆除。公共领域 过去的五角大楼预算文件和国会拨款法案已经强调了更换康涅狄格州弓形声纳罩的预期成本和复杂性。
2021 年，立法者批准了 1000 万美元专门用于圆顶的资金，以及 4000 万美元用于其他“紧急维修”。全部维修费用仍不得而知，但预计将远高于 5000 万美元。 在 2024 年发布的 2025 财年预算提案中，海军还概述了购买额外船首圆顶的计划，以防其任何一艘“海狼”级潜艇再次遭受类似的严重事故。 “海狼级潜艇的保障战略不包括提供替换潜艇

【原文 English Original】
TWZ has obtained new details about the ongoing repairs to the Seawolf class submarine USS Connecticut following collision with an underwater seamount in the South China Sea in 2021. The Navy had been looking at a roughly three-year timeline for the construction of a replacement bow sonar dome. In the end, it took just under a year for it to be built. The overall schedule for repairs to Connecticut has suffered delays, and we were the first to report that the boat is now not expected to return to service until next summer. Editor’s note: After this story was published, Janicki Industries reached out to us to ask that the image of the dome be taken down while an additional review is conducted. Out of courtesy, we agreed, and we will repost it if and when it is fully approved. Janicki Industries produced the new bow sonar dome in approximately 10 months and delivered it to the Navy in 2024, the company told us today. Janicki has a history of producing “sonar domes and precision machined hardware” for U.S. nuclear submarine programs, according to its website . It has also supported various high-profile aerospace programs, including the B-21 Raider bomber and F-35 Joint Strike Fighter . Connecticut ’s bow had initially remained attached, at least to some degree, following the collision five years ago, according to a heavily redacted Navy report on the accident . However, the entire bow structure subsequently broke away as the submarine limped to Guam . The boat then sailed to San Diego, California , and then to the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS-IMF) in Washington State, where it has been ever since. USS Connecticut seen at the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility in 2023 with its bow dome prominently missing. USN “Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & IMF [Intermediate Maintenance Facility] needed a precision replacement dome with no production line behind it, on the boat’s schedule,” Janicki also says on its website at the time of writing . “Janicki delivered it 24 months faster than the next-best option because everything the job needed sits under one roof: 5-axis mills that fit a hemisphere, the metrology to prove it, and the 1,000-ton press that forms double-curved plate.” The picture seen in part at the top of this story and in full below shows one of Janicki’s proprietary five-axis milling machines at work on the dome. The size and complexity of the bow sonar dome on Seawolf class submarines cannot be overstated. The bow sonar arrays on these boats is 24 feet in diameter. The structure of the dome itself has to be built to very exacting specifications for the sonar system to work properly. A look at the bow sonar array on a Seawolf class submarine with its bow dome removed. Public Domain Past Pentagon budget documents and appropriations bills from Congress had already highlighted the expected costs and complexities of replacing Connecticut ’s bow sonar dome. In 2021, lawmakers approved $10 million in funding specifically for the dome, as well as $40 million for other “emergent repairs.” The full repair bill is still unknown, but is expected to be far steeper than just $50 million. In its Fiscal Year 2025 budget proposal , released in 2024, the Navy also outlined plans to acquire an additional bow dome in case any of its Seawolf class submarines suffered another similarly severe mishap. “The Seawolf Class submarines sustainment strategy did not include the provisioning of replacement bow domes; therefore, no replacement bow domes for these in-service submarines are within the Navy’s inventory,” the budget documents explained. “This program would procure one Seawolf Class bow dome for use in the event replacement is required. Funds in FY25 are to purchase a bow dome which has a three plus year lead time.” Note here the mention of a lead time of at least three years, which is in line with Janicki’s statement that the “next-best option” would have taken two years more to do this work. As TWZ has highlighted in years of reporting now, repairs to Connecticut , in general, were always set to be challenging and costly due to the small size of the Seawolf class and the design being long out of production. The Navy originally planned to acquire 29 of these boats, but ultimately bought just three as a result of post-Cold War drawdowns. In addition, shrinking the program of record so severely caused the unit price of each one to rise substantially, just over $10 billion in 2025 dollars. At the time of writing, they are still the most costly attack submarines ever built. The last of the Seawolf class submarines, the highly secretive USS Jimmy Carter , which entered service in 2005, is also a heavily modified sub-type optimized for underwater espionage missions . USS Connecticut at sea in 2009. USN It is also worth noting that the U.S. Navy, as well as some of its foreign counterparts , have repaired similarly severe damage to submarines by cannibalizing entire sections from decommissioned boats in the same class. However, this is not an option given the size of the Seawolf class and the still very high demand for them operationally . The core design offers advanced capabilities that make even USS Seawolf and USS Connecticut especially well suited to a variety of specialized tasks . This is clearly why the Navy has continued to invest so much in returning Connecticut to the fleet. As mentioned, repairs to Connecticut are now not expected to be finished until sometime in the summer of next year. This is the latest in a succession of schedule slips in recent years. The original goal had been for the boat to be back in service by September 2025. “The Navy’s target completion date for the availability is the summer of 2027. PSNS & IMF is dedicated to executing this work with the highest standards of safety, technical accuracy, and craftsmanship to ensure the ship returns to the fleet ready to take its place at the tip of the spear in defense of our nation’s interests,” a Navy official told TWZ in September. “Current work consists of structural and systems restoration and required lifecycle maintenance.” Earlier in the year, the Navy also revealed that it is now planning on sending Connecticut into retirement in 2031. This means the submarine has just four more years of service ahead of it if the current repair schedule holds. The Navy does have plans to acquire a new class of nuclear attack submarines, currently referred to as SSN(X). In the past, the service has described those future boats as more of a direct successor to the Seawolf class than the versions of the Virginia class it is buying now. A picture of the first-in-class USS Seawolf . USN “The analytical conclusion was unequivocal: to dominate high-end peer threats in the middle of this century, a clean sheet design is required. The Virginia class is a fantastic, unmatched world-class warship, and it will remain the backbone of our attack fleet for decades,” Navy Rear Adm. Andrew Miller said at the Naval Submarine League’s main annual conference last week, per USNI News . “As adversary capabilities evolve, we require expanded payload capacity, greater electrical and hydrodynamic margins and unprecedented architectural flexibility that simply cannot be backfitted into an existing hull form.” Miller is currently the head of the Undersea Warfare Division with the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations. In terms of desired key capabilities for SSN(X), the Navy wants “first, higher flank speed and tactical control speed. Two, improved operational availability. Three, decisive lethality. Four, superior stealth and layered survivability, and finally organic robotic and autonomous systems hosting and command and control,” Miller added. “We are redefining the role of the submarine from a standalone hunter-killer to a capital mothership. By launching uncrewed systems directly from submarine torpedo tubes and integrating unmanned [robotic] vehicles into our battle plans, we dramatically expand the tactical reach of our manned fleet.” The first SSN(X) submarines are not expected to begin entering service until the mid-2040s, at the earliest. The Navy will continue acquiring Virginia class submarines in the interim. This includes stretched Block IV and V versions with Virginia Payload Modules (VPM) that will now be categorized as guided-missile types (SSGN). There will also be a one-of-a-kind seabed warfare version of the Virginia , which could well take over for the USS Jimmy Carter. A briefing slide from General Dynamics Electric Boat detailing existing and future planned subvariants of the Virginia class nuclear submarine. The Block VI and V types have now been reclassified as nuclear-powered guided missile submarines (SSGN) rather than nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSN). General Dynamics Electric Boat When it comes to USS Connecticut , if there are no further delays, the fully repaired submarine with its new bow sonar dome should be back in service by the middle of next year. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post New Bow Sonar Dome For Heavily Damaged Submarine USS Connecticut Seen For The First Time (Updated) appeared first on TWZ .

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

美國芯片巨頭英偉達前CEO黃仁勳身陷和疑似中共間諜女子的婚外情風波，引發美國當局質疑英偉達是否違規向中共國企業輸送芯片，從而展開調查。示意圖。（宋碧龍／大紀元）
【大紀元2026年11月17日訊】（大紀元記者李平綜合報導）美國芯片巨頭英偉達前CEO黃仁勳身陷和疑似中共間諜女子的婚外情風波，引發美國當局質疑英偉達是否違規向中共國企業輸送芯片，從而展開調查。而媒體最新披露的消息指向英偉達前長期銷售主管傑伊‧普里（Jay Puri）。
知情人士對The Information透露，過去多年來，英偉達的重要客戶，無論是購買芯片，還是需要公司特別關照，都會找普里處理，其中包括黃樂（Alice Huang）。她是黃仁勳婚外情的女主之一，涉嫌規避美國出口管制，祕密向中共走私至少75億美元英偉達AI芯片。
此外，普里還與另一家重要客戶——服務器製造商超微電腦（Supermicro）關係密切。超微多名高管今年3月因涉嫌將英偉達芯片偷運給中共被美國刑事起訴。
目前，美國司法部牽頭對英偉達展開調查，重點查明哪些客戶非法將芯片轉運給中共。與此同時，英偉達董事會也已啟動內部調查，調查黃仁勳與黃樂之間的關係。
美國政府和英偉達董事會目前重點調查黃樂，主要調查她是否將黃仁勳告訴她的信息轉交給中共情報機構。與她有關聯的公司能夠在美國法律禁止的情況下，大量向中共走私英偉達芯片，外界質疑英偉達高層是否對此視而不見。
美國限制英偉達芯片出口，目的是防止中共AI發展追趕Anthropic、OpenAI等美國企業。但中共企業仍通過走私網絡獲得大量英偉達芯片，其中一些走私公司與黃樂有關聯。此外，中共企業還利用各類雲服務商，繞過美國出口限制，從中國境外獲取英偉達芯片算力。
黃樂曾以新加坡芯片公司Megaspeed高管身分，利用與黃仁勳的親密關係大量採購英偉達芯片。然而，還有多家大量向中共輸入芯片的企業與黃樂有關聯，其中有些投資了中國AI開發商DeepSeek並向其大量供應英偉達Blackwell芯片（出口限制芯片之一）。
普里現年72歲，擁有加州理工學院電機工程碩士學位和哈佛大學工商管理碩士學位。加入英偉達之前，普里曾在惠普（Hewlett-Packard）、博思艾倫漢密爾頓（Booz Allen Hamilton）和德州儀器（Texas Instruments）工作，隨後在太陽微系統公司（Sun Microsystems）任職22年，期間擔任過多個職務，包括亞太區集團高級副總裁。
普里在英偉達任職20多年，其中17年擔任全球業務運營執行副總裁，直接向黃仁勳匯報，被視為是黃仁勳的左膀右臂。今年8月底，普里卸下日常管理職務，目前擔任英偉達顧問。
多名曾與普里密切共事的人士向The Information表示，在英偉達內部，普里被認為是推動公司從面向消費者的遊戲品牌轉型為全球AI巨頭的重要人物，幫助英偉達成為全球大型企業的芯片供應商。
普里在加州洛斯阿爾托斯（Los Altos）擁有一處住所，距英偉達總部約10英里。他卸任後，由微軟前高管尼克‧帕克（Nick Parker）接任英偉達銷售主管一職。
The Information報導，目前雖沒有證據指向普里存在不當行為或違規活動，但他與黃仁勳及英偉達主要客戶關係如此密切，很可能成為調查人員約談對象。
英偉達最大的直接客戶是戴爾（Dell）、超微電腦等設備製造商。這些公司將英偉達芯片組裝成服務器，再出售給雲服務商及其他大型客戶。
The Information報導，普里的妻子陳森麗（Cenly Chen，音譯）曾長期擔任超微電腦高層，兩人婚姻關係是兩人親口告訴同事。據內部人士以及超微股東針對公司及其高管提起的民事訴訟文件，陳森麗曾是超微與英偉達關係管理團隊成員，直接向超微首席執行官梁見後匯報。
多名曾參與英偉達服務器銷售業務的人士向The Information透露，普里與陳森麗多年來一直關係密切，兩人曾於2024年一同出席舊金山歌劇院舉辦的慈善晚會，並被拍下合影。但目前無法確認兩人什麼時候結婚。
The Information報導，一名證券法律師指出，普里在擔任英偉達高管期間與在超微電腦任職的陳森麗結婚或同居，英偉達就應依法在證券申報文件中披露雙方關係。但英偉達提交的文件沒有透露這一點，英偉達對此說法也拒絕置評，只多次表示公司遵守美國法律。
超微電腦曾是英偉達最大的客戶之一。公司兩名高管涉嫌協助將英偉達先進AI芯片轉運給中共，今年3月被起訴，罪名是合謀將美國政府禁止出口的英偉達服務器走私給中共，兩人隨後離職。
陳森麗當時擔任超微高級副總裁兼首席增長官，但未被指控有任何不當行為。陳森麗領英（LinkedIn）信息顯示，她於今年4月離職，距離案件曝光約一個月。陳目前擔任上市AI雲服務商Chronoscale首席執行官，該公司是英偉達雲合作夥伴（Nvidia Cloud Partner），能夠優先獲得英偉達芯片。
多名了解英偉達AI芯片銷售情況的人士向The Information表示，普里決定英偉達向超微電腦及其他服務器製造商出售AI芯片的數量。另一方面，超微股東訴訟文件顯示，陳森麗曾參與決定超微電腦如何向客戶分配搭載英偉達芯片的服務器機櫃。還有陳的前同事稱，陳森麗實際上就是超微銷售主管。對此超微一概否認。
The Information報導，超微股東民事起訴書顯示，一名前超微電腦銷售總監曾向股東揭示，陳曾發電子郵件要求英偉達放行的一批芯片序列號，與此前被非法轉運給中共客戶手中的GPU有關。
據一名曾與陳共事的人士向The Information透露，多家服務中國客戶的英偉達芯片轉售商都和陳認識，或曾試圖與她建立密切關係。普里和陳森麗均未回應The Information置評請求。+

zh_title: 在全球舞台上预防疾病：海军医护兵反思《太平洋伙伴关系 2026》
summary: **加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村** — 从在越南培训公共卫生官员到在印度尼西亚教授食品卫生和疾病预防，分配到海军医学准备和训练司令部 (NMRTC) 二十九棕榈村的一名海军预防医学技术人员在 2026 年太平洋伙伴关系期间帮助加强了国际伙伴关系并保护部署人员的健康。 医院医护兵一等兵肖恩·迈克尔·韦默 (Sean Michael Weimer) 是加利福尼亚州莫德斯托人，于 6 月至 7 月参加了多国人道主义援助和备灾任务2026年，一起工作
content:
**加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村** — 从在越南培训公共卫生官员到在印度尼西亚教授食品卫生和疾病预防，分配到海军医学准备和训练司令部 (NMRTC) 二十九棕榈村的一名海军预防医学技术人员在 2026 年太平洋伙伴关系期间帮助加强了国际伙伴关系并保护了部署人员的健康。

一级医院医护兵肖恩·迈克尔·韦默 (Sean Michael Weimer) 是加利福尼亚州莫德斯托人，参加了 2026 年 6 月至 7 月的多国人道主义援助和备灾任务，与美国陆军医疗专家、澳大利亚和印度尼西亚军事人员以及来自多个伙伴国家的公共卫生专业人员合作，分享预防医学实践并降低疾病风险。

对于担任 NMRTC 二十九棕榈村公共卫生局首席士官的韦默来说，这次任务提供了一个机会，可以运用他在环境健康和疾病预防方面的经验，同时与印度太平洋地区的社区建立关系。

韦默说：“太平洋伙伴关系强调了任务准备工作在多大程度上取决于在疾病发生之前预防疾病。” “保持人员健康可以让他们继续工作并支持我们访问的社区。”
韦默于 6 月在越南洞海开始了他的任务，在那里他与美国陆军昆虫学家和微生物学家一起工作，为当地疾病控制中心的越南公共卫生官员提供专门培训。

培训重点是蚊子和蜱虫识别、监测技术和杀虫剂抗药性测试，为参与者提供了监测携带疾病的昆虫和加强当地疾病预防工作的实用知识。

在越南工作结束后，魏默前往菲律宾苏比克湾，在那里登上澳大利亚皇家海军舰艇 HMAS Choules，转机前往印度尼西亚西博尔加。在船上期间，魏默能够与澳大利亚皇家水手一起参加大规模伤亡演习，进一步加深了他的互操作经验。

在整个任务期间，魏默担任预防医学技术员，负责约 150 名人员的部队健康保护。他的职责包括提供食品和水安全、卫生、蚊虫叮咬预防和传染病风险方面的指导。

他还对部署人员进行了有关区域健康威胁的教育，包括疟疾和登革热，强调可以减少疾病并帮助保持行动准备状态的预防措施。

韦默说：“保护团队的健康有助于使任务顺利进行，而培训交流则为我们提供了分享实用技能和相互学习的机会。”
7月，韦默与美国陆军兽医和食品检验员一起在锡博尔加在当地学校、学院、动物农场和屠宰场进行公共卫生培训。

该团队提供了有关食品卫生、正确洗手和畜牧业的指导，分享了减少疾病传播和改善社区健康的实用方法。

虽然培训的重点是基本的预防医学实践，但韦默表示，与当地居民直接互动的机会使这次经历特别有意义。

【原文 English Original】
**TWENTYNINE PALMS, Calif.** — From training public health officials in Vietnam to teaching food sanitation and disease prevention in Indonesia, a Navy preventive medicine technician assigned to Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command (NMRTC) Twentynine Palms helped strengthen international partnerships and protect the health of deployed personnel during Pacific Partnership 2026.

Hospital Corpsman 1st Class Sean Michael Weimer, a native of Modesto, California, participated in the multinational humanitarian assistance and disaster preparedness mission from June to July 2026, working alongside U.S. Army medical specialists, Australian and Indonesian military personnel and public health professionals from several partner nations to share preventive medicine practices and reduce the risk of disease.

For Weimer, who serves as the leading petty officer for the directorate for public health at NMRTC Twentynine Palms, the mission offered an opportunity to apply his experience in environmental health and disease prevention while building relationships with communities across the Indo-Pacific.

“Pacific Partnership reinforced how much mission readiness depends on preventing illness before it occurs,” Weimer said. “Keeping personnel healthy allows them to continue their work and support communities we visit.”

Weimer began his mission in June in Dong Hoi, Vietnam, where he worked alongside U.S. Army entomologists and microbiologists to provide specialized training to Vietnamese public health officials at a local disease control center.

The training focused on mosquito and tick identification, surveillance techniques and insecticide resistance testing, providing participants with practical knowledge to monitor disease-carrying insects and strengthen local disease prevention efforts.

Following his work in Vietnam, Weimer traveled to Subic Bay, Philippines, where he boarded the Royal Australian Navy ship HMAS Choules for a transit to Sibolga, Indonesia. During his time aboard, Weimer was able to participate in a mass casualty exercise alongside Royal Australian sailors, furthering his interoperability experience.

Throughout the mission, Weimer served as a preventive medicine technician responsible for force health protection for approximately 150 personnel. His duties included providing guidance on food and water safety, sanitation, mosquito bite prevention and communicable disease risks.

He also educated deployed personnel about regional health threats, including malaria and dengue fever, emphasizing preventive measures that could reduce illness and help sustain operational readiness.

“Protecting the team’s health helped keep the mission on track, while the training exchanges gave us opportunities to share practical skills and learn from one another,” Weimer said.

In July, Weimer joined U.S. Army veterinarians and food inspectors in Sibolga to conduct public health training at local schools, colleges, animal farms and a slaughterhouse.

The team provided instruction on food sanitation, proper handwashing and animal husbandry, sharing practical methods to reduce disease transmission and improve community health.

While the training focused on fundamental preventive medicine practices, Weimer said the opportunity to interact directly with local residents made the experience particularly meaningful.

“Sibolga, Indonesia, stood out to me the most,” Weimer said. “Although the community had limited resources, the people were incredibly friendly, welcoming and happy to have us there.”

Working in schools and other community facilities allowed Weimer and his fellow medical professionals to exchange knowledge with residents while developing relationships that extended beyond the training itself.

“What stayed with me the most was their kindness and enthusiasm,” Weimer said. “It reminded me that building relationships is just as meaningful as the training we provide.”

Collaboration with allied and partner nation personnel was another important aspect of the mission. Working alongside members of the military and public health professionals from different countries exposed Weimer to varying approaches to disease prevention, environmental health and medical readiness.

He said differences in available resources, regional disease threats and the organization of public health services created opportunities for participants to learn from one another.

“Our partners brought valuable knowledge of the diseases and environmental conditions they dealt with regularly,” Weimer said. “We shared our experience with surveillance, standardized procedures and protecting personnel in an operational setting.”

The exchange reinforced the importance of adapting preventive medicine practices to local conditions rather than relying on a single approach.

At NMRTC Twentynine Palms, Weimer oversees 18 environmental health programs supporting Marines, Sailors, staff and beneficiaries across Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center Twentynine Palms.

Those programs include food safety, drinking water surveillance, vector and pest management, immunizations, communicable disease surveillance and sanitation. He also leads and develops hospital corpsmen and preventive medicine technicians, helping prepare personnel to meet operational requirements.

Weimer said his responsibilities at Twentynine Palms provided a foundation for the work he performed overseas, particularly when delivering instruction to audiences with different levels of public health experience.

“My work at NMRTC Twentynine Palms gave me a strong foundation in food safety, water surveillance, sanitation and disease prevention,” Weimer said. “These are areas I work with regularly, so I was able to apply that experience during the mission and explain those practices to different audiences.”

His experience training corpsmen and preventive medicine technicians also helped prepare him to teach at schools, colleges and other facilities throughout the deployment.

Weimer's path to preventive medicine began in a different Navy career field. He originally served as an aviation boatswain's mate before converting to hospital corpsman in search of new professional opportunities.

He eventually pursued preventive medicine because of its emphasis on protecting entire populations rather than focusing exclusively on individual patient care.

“Preventive medicine was a field that really interested me because of its focus on preventing illness and protecting the health of entire groups of people,” Weimer said.

Pacific Partnership 2026 marked Weimer's first humanitarian mission, providing a new perspective on how Navy Medicine personnel can contribute to operational readiness and international cooperation through disease prevention, education and community engagement.

The experience also demonstrated how preventive medicine can serve as a foundation for building trust with partner nations while addressing shared public health challenges.

“In Sibolga, teaching practical skills like food sanitation and handwashing gave us opportunities to connect with the community and build trust,” Weimer said. “Those relationships made the work especially meaningful to me.”

Weimer's contributions during Pacific Partnership 2026 reflect Navy Medicine's commitment to advancing global health, strengthening interoperability with allies and partner nations, and maintaining medical readiness in support of operational missions. These efforts also support the Defense Health Agency's mission to deliver ready medical capabilities to the joint force while strengthening cooperation and improving health outcomes on the global stage.

For other corpsmen and military medical professionals considering participation in future humanitarian missions, Weimer encouraged them to embrace opportunities to work in unfamiliar environments and learn from the people they encounter.

“Go with an open mind, be flexible and willing to learn from your partners and the community,” Weimer said. “Be prepared to adapt what you know to local conditions and available resources.”

Reflecting on his experience, Weimer said the relationships developed during the mission were among its most lasting contributions.

“Take time to get to know the people you are supporting,” Weimer said. “For me, those connections were one of the most rewarding parts of the mission and gave me a broader perspective on what we can accomplish through Navy Medicine.”

Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command Twentynine Palms operates Defense Health Agency military treatment facility Naval Hospital Twentynine Palms, which delivers safe, high-quality healthcare to service members and their families. The command supports the health and readiness of warfighters at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center Twentynine Palms, the Marine Corps' largest live-fire training installation, while readying Navy Medicine personnel to provide expeditionary medical support around the world.

content:
科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”董 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县推广 职称 推广区域专家 会员等级 高级会员 母校内蒙古师范大学，位于呼和浩特；北京师范大学；纽约州立大学环境科学与林业学院，位于锡拉丘兹；科罗拉多州立大学全球分校 她构建了人工智能驱动的农业旅游聊天机器人 (AgriTourismAI.com)，帮助农民和牧场主启动和经营“农业旅游”业务。农业旅游是指农民向游客开放他们的土地以进行娱乐、教育或购物活动。常见的例子包括采摘自己的果园、如何种植蔬菜的课程以及手工产品的销售。董还举办研讨会，向农民和牧场主展示如何使用人工智能工具来帮助发展和管理他们的业务。她说她将自己视为大学和农村之间的纽带。 “我们（推广专家）充当桥梁，”她说。
“我们将校园与我们服务的农村社区联系起来。”许多农民和牧场主年龄较大，通常没有接受过技术培训。他们的子孙常常离开农场到城市工作，或者无法教他们新工具。如果没有帮助，人工智能的好处可能会与农民失之交臂。 Dong 的研讨会为他们提供了一条出路。Dong 凭借她的 AgriPivot AI Agent 入围 2026 年 GenAI for Good Challenge 决赛。该挑战赛由 IEEE Humanarian Technologies 和联合国国际电信联盟组织，她的项目是从 79 个国家的 318 个团队中选出的。她还获得了国家推广技术社区 (NETC) 颁发的 2026 年创新奖，以及国家社区发展推广专业人员协会 (NACDEP) 颁发的 2025 年国家和西部地区教育技术奖。作为首席研究员或联合首席研究员，她获得了七项竞争性资助，总额超过 25 万美元，其中包括由农业部国家食品和农业研究所支持的资金。董出生于北京，从小就热爱设计和解决问题。她的父母都是医生。小时候，她喜欢画新的、有创意的东西。她说，素描可以让她用图片解决脑海中的问题，并将它们作为实际设计写在纸上。这个习惯逐渐成为她与周围环境相处的一种方式。
她说：“我一直热衷于创造一些有形的东西来解决现实世界中的问题。”她并不将自己的人生方向归功于任何一位导师。相反，她说她所有的老师都帮助她为她的职业生涯奠定了基础。她就读于位于呼和浩特的内蒙古师范大学，这是一所培训教师的机构。 2013 年，她在那里获得了两个学士学位——一个是地理科学学士学位，另一个是教育学士学位。然后，她获得了课程和教学硕士学位

【原文 English Original】
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

关岛阿加纳高地——美国海军医疗准备和训练司令部 (USNMRTC) 关岛的一支远征医疗队最近在亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰 (CVN 72) 上部署后返回家园。

重症监护护士 Jose Tolentino 中尉和飞行途中护理兼一般值勤护理人员一等医院医护员 Luis Nazareno 组成了途中护理系统 (ERCS) 3 团队。他们的主要任务是为医疗后送提供先进的医疗能力，同时完全融入船舶的日常医疗运营。

托伦蒂诺说：“对于 ERCS 团队来说，典型的一天首先是确保设备和物资准备就绪，以防我们需要进行医疗后送。” “我们支持早晨病假电话、飞行甲板战斗更衣站值班、晚上病假电话以及全天出现的任何医疗紧急情况。”

纳扎雷诺是一位经验丰富的水手，正在进行第九次部署并具备全套资格，他指出该团队很快就成为了船舶节奏的一部分。纳扎雷诺从第一天起就担任导师并担任值班部门负责人。他的经验和资历使他能够立即担任关键的值班职务。他报到后不久就帮助驾驶舱战备站值班，值班时间超过1000小时，保障了驾驶舱人员的安全。
“我们很容易融入船舶的运营，”纳扎雷诺说。 “每当他们需要帮助时，我们都会很乐意在等待他们执行主要医疗后送任务时提供帮助。”

他们的资格也转化为船舶的整体医疗准备情况。 Tolentino 担任林肯美国红十字会生命支持项目 (CPR/BLS) 的项目经理，领导 21 名讲师并管理 82 个生命支持课程。

纳扎雷诺在数百名水手成功获得心肺复苏和战术战斗伤亡护理 (TCCC) 认证方面发挥了至关重要的作用。托伦蒂诺还担任战术战斗伤亡护理教练。这些努力显着增加了船上能够有效应对医疗紧急情况的水兵人数。

该小组还在部署期间进行了多次医疗后送，包括拯救一名呼吸困难的平民渔民。

纳扎雷诺描述了另一个复杂的案例，涉及四辆不同车辆和人员之间的协调转移。

“这确实证明了美国海军的灵活性和后勤协调性，”他说。

此次部署强化了有关手术医学的几个关键经验教训，这些经验教训直接影响了团队如何照顾水手和支持船舶。在海上，他们必须足智多谋，在物资有限的情况下做出决定，并跳出框框思考。
“手术医学确实与医院环境‘相同但不同’，”纳扎雷诺解释道。 “药物本质上是一样的，但演示和执行可能需要开箱即用的思维。”

托伦蒂诺表示同意并表示：“我学会了如何利用船上有限的资源来提供护理，以及为面临后勤挑战的时期做好计划的重要性。”

尽管船上生活有独特的限制，这些课程使团队能够为船上的水手提供有效的护理和培训。

与全船各个部门的水手一起工作留下了持久的印象。

“从提供膳食的烹饪专家到大妈，每个部门在确保部署成功方面都发挥着关键作用

【原文 English Original】
AGANA HEIGHTS, GUAM – An Expeditionary Medicine team from U.S. Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command (USNMRTC) Guam recently returned home after deploying aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72).

Lt. Jose Tolentino, a critical care nurse, and Hospital Corpsman 1st Class Luis Nazareno, a flight enroute care and general duty corpsman, formed the En Route Care System (ERCS) 3 team. Their primary mission was to deliver advanced medical capability for medical evacuations while integrating fully into the ship’s daily medical operations.

“A typical day for the ERCS team began with ensuring equipment and supplies were ready in case we were called upon for a medevac,” Tolentino said. “We supported morning sick call, flight deck battle dressing station watch, evening sick call, and any medical emergencies that arose throughout the day.”

Nazareno, a seasoned Sailor on his ninth deployment and the full set of qualifications, noted the team quickly became part of the ship’s rhythm. Nazareno served as a mentor and assumed the role of duty section lead from day one. His experience and qualifications allowed him to step into critical watch standing roles immediately. He helped stand the flight deck battle dressing station watch shortly after reporting aboard and stood more than 1,000 hours of watch, ensuring the safety of flight deck personnel.

“We integrated into the ship’s operations easily,” Nazareno said. “Whenever they needed help, we gladly offered while we waited to be utilized for our primary medevac mission.”

Their qualifications also translated into the ship’s overall medical readiness. Tolentino assumed the role of program manager for Lincoln’s American Red Cross Life Support Programs (CPR/BLS, leading 21 instructors and managing 82 life support classes.

Nazareno played a vital role in the successful certification of hundreds of Sailors in CPR and Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC). Tolentino also served as a Tactical Combat Casualty Care instructor. These efforts significantly expanded the number of Sailors aboard who could respond effectively to medical emergencies.

The team also conducted several medevacs during the deployment, including saving a civilian fisherman in respiratory distress.

Nazareno described another complex case involving coordinated transfers across four different vehicles and crews.

“It was really a testament to the flexibility and logistical coordination of the U.S. Navy,” he said.

The deployment reinforced several key lessons about operational medicine that directly shaped how the team cared for Sailors and supported the ship. At sea, they had to be resourceful, make decisions with limited supplies, and think outside the box.

“Operational medicine really is ‘same but different’ from the hospital setting,” Nazareno explained. “The medicine is fundamentally the same, but the presentation and execution may need out-of-the-box thinking.”

Tolentino agreed and said, “I learned how to use the limited resources aboard a ship to provide care and the importance of planning for periods with logistical challenges.”

These lessons enabled the team to deliver effective care and training to the Sailors aboard the ship, despite the unique constraints of shipboard life.

Working alongside Sailors from every department throughout the ship left a lasting impression.

“Every department plays a critical role in ensuring a successful deployment, from the culinary specialists providing meals to the damage controlmen troubleshooting equipment,” Tolentino said.

Nazareno added that the Lincoln’s crew welcomed them with open arms.

For Tolentino, it was his first shipboard deployment. He relied heavily on Nazareno’s extensive experience and the ship’s hospital corpsmen who taught him the nuances of shipboard patient care, charting, and working across medical departments from radiology to the laboratory.

Morale remained high through shipboard programs. Wi-Fi allowed Sailors to stay connected with family. The ship’s Morale, Welfare and Recreation team, known as the “Fun Boss,” organized talent shows, dance lessons, and painting events, while the “Fit Boss” led fitness challenges, run club, and high-intensity interval training classes.

Life at sea also brought challenges, including delay in receiving mail and limited workout spaces. Nazareno simply observed, “You really can survive without your personal electronics.”

The deployment tested their resilience when the original return date slipped repeatedly into the summer.

“I learned to become more fluid and not focus on things outside my control,” Tolentino said.

Nazareno agreed. “Not knowing when the finish line was a challenge. However, by being positive and focusing on the tasks at hand, long deployments become easier.”

When the ship finally approached Guam, the reality of homecoming set in.

“It seemed unreal,” Tolentino said. “I still didn’t believe we were coming home until we were actually days out from Guam.”

Nazareno summed up with a seasoned Sailor’s perspective.

“Port isn’t real until feet are on the ground.”

Reuniting with family brought powerful moments. Tolentino’s 12-year-old son cried upon seeing him on the pier. Both expressed deep gratitude for the support they received from USNMRTC Guam.

“The command acted and responded promptly whenever I reached out,” Tolentino said. “My spouse works in the hospital laboratory, and her leadership helped manage her schedule and workload while she held things down at home. Leadership from the hospital and the Emergency Department even met us on the pier on a weekend. That gesture brought real meaning to the word ‘family."

Nazareno echoed the appreciation.

“Every bit of administrative and logistical support made our lives easier and allowed us to focus on the mission,” Nazareno said. “And the coffee that was sent really was a lifesaver in the early months.”

For the command’s leadership, the successful deployment of the ERCS team represents the real-world application of the Expeditionary Medicine readiness capabilities.

“The entire command is very proud that our own Lt. Tolentino and Hospital Corpsman 1st Class Nazareno supported the USS Abraham Lincoln deployment,” said Captain James Demitrack, commanding officer of USNTRC Guam. “Our command is responsible for eight Expeditionary Medicine platforms, and these units help to make us who we are. The complex patient care that our providers, nurses and corpsmen provide at our hospital supports the readiness of these teams. The presence of these teams here in Guam makes it clear to all of our staff that our command is critical to the operational readiness of the entire Navy.”

Both Sailors return with valuable experience they intend to share with their command — practical medevac expertise, greater flexibility, and the knowledge that an upbeat attitude makes even the longest deployments more manageable.

U.S. Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command Guam directly sustains Navy and Marine Corps operational readiness, preparing its medical forces to deliver critical medical support to maritime and expeditionary forces, ashore or at sea, anytime and anywhere.

title: 遭美制裁高校買英偉達芯片 含國防七子成員

content:
【大紀元2026年11月20日訊】（大紀元記者李言綜合報導）最新審查的商業與採購記錄顯示，近年來至少有六所遭美國列入出口管制「實體清單」（Entity List）黑名單的中國大學，報告採購了受限制的英偉達（Nvidia）芯片，其中包含與中共軍方關係密切的「國防七子」成員。
美國有線電視新聞網（CNN）檢視了約300份中國高校與機構的採購文件，發現多數涉及受美方管制的A100、A800、H100、H200及H800等芯片。
在明確點名的高校中，屬於「國防七子」的哈爾濱工業大學今年9月報告以約7,000美元購入一枚A100芯片；同屬該群體的西北工業大學今年9月與10月則有兩份公告，顯示購入共四枚H200芯片，總價約24萬美元；另一所「國防七子」高校北京航空航天大學，也在2022年至2024年間報告逾十筆採購，以A100和A800為主。
此外，另有三所「實體清單」大學近年也報告採購高端英偉達芯片。在CNN審查的90家買家中，近80%是大學，近14%是研究所，此外政府機構也購買了一些英偉達芯片。
專家指出，這些交易多透過中國本土不知名賣家進行，規模相對有限，但凸顯受限芯片在中國境內仍具流通性，且美方難以完全阻斷高風險實體的獲取渠道。前美國出口管制官員凱特‧科倫（Kate Koren）向CNN表示，芯片一旦進入中國便極難阻止轉售，走私網絡常藉助空殼公司、多地轉運與偽造文件規避查緝。
路透社（Reuters）此前披露，自2001年便被列入美國「實體清單」的西北工業大學，今年10月透過本土供應商「陝西博算網絡科技有限公司」為管理學院採購兩枚H200芯片，金額為87.47萬元人民幣。
報導也提到，該校今年還曾與多家中國本土科技供應商簽訂算力租賃合同，以使用H200等高性能芯片。美方雖於今年1月調整H200對華出口審查規則，改為逐案評估，但並未解除針對「實體清單」機構的限制。+

title: The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit
zh_title: 美国参加2026年东亚峰会
summary: 发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为在美国与东盟建立关系50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《落实美国-东盟领导人共识的全面工作计划》
content:
发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为了在美国-东盟关系成立50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《实施美国-东盟领导人共同愿景声明的综合工作计划，以促进东盟和美国更强大、更安全和更繁荣》（2026-2030年）。美国强调其与盟友和伙伴一道致力于加强威慑，以维护印太地区的和平与稳定。在两国建交80周年之际，美国祝贺菲律宾成功担任东盟轮值主席国。促进和平，加强自由开放的印太地区 美国将继续在印太地区发挥领导作用，并威慑该地区任何试图通过武力解决争端的国家，这体现了特朗普总统通过实力实现和平的承诺。
美国将继续维护《联合国海洋法公约》所反映的国际法规定的所有国家行使航行和飞越自由的权利，包括在南中国海。台海的和平与稳定对于印太地区的安全与繁荣仍然至关重要，美国反对任何单方面改变现状的行为。美国仍然致力于实现朝鲜完全无核化，并全面执行联合国安理会所有涉朝决议。扩大贸易、能源和技术联系美国仍然是东盟最大的单一国家外国直接投资者，截至 2025 年，该地区的外国直接投资超过 5,570 亿美元，为美国提供了约 532,000 个就业岗位。美国祝贺东盟领导人签署《数字经济框架协议》，该协议有可能为美国科技公司提供更大的机会，让该地区的数字经济到2030年将达到2万亿美元。随着美国超级智能（SI）技术在全球树立黄金标准，美国正在与东南亚伙伴合作，扩大获得美国技术的机会，包括通过美国-东盟SI SPARK计划，这将有助于释放该地区的经济潜力。
通过签署《人工智能机会声明》，越南和柬埔寨与其他国家一道致力于促进基于可信赖伙伴关系的创新。为了支持该地区的人工智能准备工作，美国将与印度尼西亚政府、东盟秘书处和卡内基梅隆大学合作，于 12 月在雅加达举办东盟人工智能周。美国和菲律宾签署了一项为期五年的经济繁荣和韧性战略目标协议，该协议将动员对包括吕宋经济走廊在内的关键基础设施的投资，并与可靠的合作伙伴一起确保供应链的安全。作为世界上最大的能源生产国之一，美国可以为东南亚几代人的增长提供动力。美国准备与东盟合作加强该地区的能源安全

【原文 English Original】
Office of the Spokesman The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit Fact Sheet November 18, 2026 At the East Asia Summit in Manila, Philippines on November 17, the United States reaffirmed its commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, expressed support for ASEAN centrality, and underscored the United States as the region’s preferred partner for energy and technology. To advance their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership ahead of the 50 th anniversary of U.S.-ASEAN relations, the United States and ASEAN adopted the Comprehensive Work Plan to Implement the U.S.-ASEAN Leaders’ Joint Vision Statement to Promote a Stronger, Safer, and More Prosperous ASEAN and America (2026-2030). The United States highlighted its commitment, with allies and partners, to strengthen deterrence to safeguard peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region. The United States congratulated the Philippines on a successful ASEAN chair year, as the two countries mark 80 years of diplomatic relations. Promoting Peace and Strengthening a Free and Open Indo-Pacific Reflecting President Trump’s commitment to peace through strength, the United States will continue to lead in the Indo-Pacific and deter any nation in the region tempted to settle disputes by force. The United States will continue to uphold the right of all nations under international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Seas (UNCLOS) to exercise freedom of navigation and overflight, including in the South China Sea. Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait remain essential to the security and prosperity of the Indo-Pacific and the United States opposes any unilateral change to the status quo. The United States remains committed to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the full implementation of all DPRK-related UN Security Council resolutions. Expanding Trade, Energy, and Technology Ties The United States remains ASEAN’s largest single country foreign direct investor, with more than $557 billion in foreign direct investment in the region as of 2025, which supports an estimated 532,000 American jobs. The United States congratulated ASEAN leaders for signing the Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which has the potential to provide U.S. technology companies with greater opportunities in the region’s digital economy projected to reach $2 trillion by 2030. As American Super Intelligence (SI) technology sets the gold standard worldwide, the United States is working with Southeast Asian partners to expand access to U.S. technology, including through the U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK program, which will help unlock the region’s economic potential. By signing the AI Opportunity Statement, Vietnam and Cambodia joined other nations in committing to fostering innovation anchored in trusted partnerships. To support the region’s SI readiness, the United States will collaborate with the Government of Indonesia, ASEAN Secretariat, and Carnegie Mellon University to host ASEAN SI Week in Jakarta in December. The United States and the Philippines signed a five-year Economic Prosperity and Resilience Strategic Objective Agreement, which will mobilize investment in critical infrastructure, including in the Luzon Economic Corridor, and secure supply chains with reliable partners. As one of the world’s largest energy producers, the United States can power Southeast Asia’s growth for generations. The United States is ready to work with ASEAN to strengthen the region’s energy security through support for the ASEAN Power Grid. The United States is sharing its 70 years of experience and leadership in nuclear energy by promoting nuclear safety, security, and nonproliferation in Southeast Asia. Building on our existing 123 Agreements with Indonesia and Vietnam, the United States has entered into 123 Agreements with the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand, and launched negotiations with Malaysia. This cooperation will help the region meet its growing energy demand, including reliable power for SI. The United States is expanding civil nuclear cooperation in Southeast Asia, where energy demand is anticipated to triple by 2050. Consistent with the U.S.-Japan-South Korea Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) on Small Modular Reactor (SMR) deployments, the United States is providing SMR control room simulators and other technical assistance to Indonesia under the Department’s Foundational Infrastructure for the Responsible Use of Small Modular Reactor Technology (FIRST) program to help establish Indonesia as a regional SMR hub. These partnerships strengthen energy security, drive economic growth, and support jobs in the United States and across the region. Combating Scams and Transnational Crime Scam groups based in Southeast Asia stole at least $18.2 billion from Americans and around $23 billion from citizens of ASEAN member states in 2025. In response, President Trump issued Executive Order 14390, titled “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” and the Department of State has confronted these criminal groups head on. The Department is directing an additional $26.2 million to train and equip Southeast Asian law enforcement and criminal justice officials to work with U.S. law enforcement to catch and prosecute scam network operators. The United States and 12 regional partners in the Contact Group to Counter Criminal Online Scams agreed to a Statement of Principles to drive joint action to dismantle the scam syndicates targeting our people. The United States and ASEAN also adopted the U.S.-ASEAN Statement on 10 Public-Private Partnership Principles for Tackling Online Scams, deepening regional and private-sector cooperation.

zh_title: 巴拿马就长和港口纠纷提起刑事诉讼
summary: 巴拿马提起与长和港口纠纷有关的刑事诉讼 2026 年 2 月 4 日，巴拿马巴拿马城，无人机拍摄的画面显示，在巴拿马最高法院宣布香港长和港口公司持有的关键港口合同无效后，巴拿马港口公司 (PPC) 停靠的集装箱，导致一些巴拿马运河业务的未来充满不确定性。路透社/Enea Lebrun 巴拿马提出了与长和港口有关的刑事诉讼路透巴拿马城11月18日 - 巴拿马审计长周三表示，已就审计中发现的涉嫌违规行为提起刑事诉讼
content:
巴拿马就长和港口纠纷提起刑事诉讼
2026 年 2 月 4 日，巴拿马巴拿马城，无人机拍摄的景象显示，在巴拿马最高法院宣布香港长和旗下公司持有的关键港口合同无效后，巴拿马港口公司 (PPC) 停靠的集装箱，使一些巴拿马运河业务的未来充满不确定性。 REUTERS/Enea Lebrun
巴拿马就长和港口纠纷提起刑事诉讼
路透巴拿马城11月18日 - 巴拿马审计长周三表示，已对与香港长和旗下子公司的国家合同审计中发现的涉嫌违规行为提起刑事诉讼。
审计长办公室表示，该投诉寻求调查与该州与长和旗下巴拿马港口公司（PPC）之间的港口特许权合同有关的可能犯罪行为。
该公司表示，该文件涵盖了 2014 年至 2023 年间巴拿马海事管理局的前董事会成员、该机构在此期间的前管理人员以及 PPC 本身。
当局和 PPC 没有立即回应置评请求。
审计长表示，该投诉源于对公司财务报表和合同义务遵守情况的审计结果。
该办公室没有详细说明涉嫌违规行为，但表示已将文件移交给检察官进行调查。
此举标志着关于PPC在巴拿马运河附近运营巴尔博亚港和克里斯托瓦尔港的角色的更广泛争议的最新进展，巴拿马运河是世界上最繁忙的海上水道之一。
今年早些时候，巴拿马取消了该公司的港口特许权，导致 PPC 和长和之间的法律和外交斗争升级。
近几个月来，PPC 还指控巴拿马当局在接管这些设施期间非法扣押财产和文件，但总统何塞·劳尔·穆利诺 (Jose Raul Mulino) 否认了这一指控。
这场纠纷使长和拟将其全球港口业务的多数股权出售给贝莱德和地中海航运公司牵头的财团的计划变得复杂。

Panama Files Criminal Complaint Tied to CK Hutchison Ports Dispute
A drone view shows containers docked at Panama Ports Company (PPC) after Panama’s Supreme Court annulled key port contracts held by the Hong Kong?based CK Hutchison–owned firm, leaving the future of some Panama Canal operations uncertain, in Panama City, Panama, February 4, 2026. REUTERS/Enea Lebrun
Panama Files Criminal Complaint Tied to CK Hutchison Ports Dispute
PANAMA CITY, Nov 18 (Reuters) – Panama’s comptroller general said on Wednesday it had filed a criminal complaint over suspected irregularities uncovered in an audit of a state contract with a unit of Hong Kong conglomerate CK Hutchison.
The comptroller’s office said the complaint seeks an investigation into possible crimes linked to the port concession contract between the state and the CK Hutchison unit, Panama Ports Company (PPC).
It said the filing covers former board members of the Panama Maritime Authority between 2014 and 2023, former administrators of the authority during that period, and PPC itself.
The authority and PPC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The complaint stems from findings in an audit of the company’s financial statements and compliance with contractual obligations, the comptroller said.
The office did not detail the suspected irregularities, but said it had turned over documentation to the public prosecutor for investigation.
The move marks the latest development in a broader dispute over PPC’s role operating the Balboa and Cristobal ports near the Panama Canal, one of the world’s busiest maritime waterways.
Earlier this year, Panama moved to unwind the company’s port concessions, escalating a legal and diplomatic fight involving PPC and CK Hutchison.
PPC has also accused Panamanian authorities in recent months of unlawfully seizing property and documents during the takeover of the facilities, allegations President Jose Raul Mulino has rejected.
The dispute has complicated CK Hutchison’s proposed sale of a majority stake in its global ports business to a consortium led by BlackRock and Mediterranean Shipping Company.
(Reporting by Elida Moreno; Writing by Anthony Esposito and Kylie Madry; editing by Cassandra Garrison)

content:
特朗普提出在中国拘留美国人的问题海峡时报
特朗普称助手因中方拘留两名美国人而被提
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，一名助手向中国官员提出了两名美国人被北京拘留的案件。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 20 日 06:25
更新于 2026 年 11 月 20 日 06:41
特朗普表示，一名助手在与习近平的深圳峰会上向中国官员提出了美国人陈友林和敏津被拘留的问题。
陈自 2024 年 11 月以来一直被关押，并被指控从事间谍活动；辛于六月前往云南参加学术会议后被捕。
他们的案件很重要，因为华盛顿称他们“被错误拘留”，而中国则表示根据自己的法律处理此类案件。
华盛顿 - 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普 11 月 19 日告诉路透社，一名助手在访问中国期间向中国官员提出了两名美国人陈友林和敏津的案件，他们被美国认定为被北京错误拘留。
特朗普在与中国和俄罗斯外长举行的深圳峰会飞回华盛顿时与路透社通了电话。
陈是一位出生于中国的地震学家，擅长探测朝鲜核试验，自 2024 年 11 月以来一直被中国关押；缅甸问题研究员辛于六月访问中国西南部期间被捕。
国务卿马可·卢比奥将这两人认定为错误拘留，这使得释放他们成为美国的首要任务。中国不承认这一指定，并表示拘留案件是根据中国法律处理的。
11 月 18 日，共和党议员敦促特朗普向习近平施压，释放两人。但特朗普告诉路透社，一名助手已向中方提出了他们的案件。
他说，这些人是被中国关押的“少数”美国人之一。
特朗普继续说道：“我们已经把很多人从很多国家释放了。”他指的是自 2025 年 1 月开始他的第二个任期以来，其他政府释放了美国人。
“你知道我从白俄罗斯和其他地方运出了数百个。”
据美国官员称，自特朗普重新上任以来，外国政府已将 115 名美国公民从国外拘留中释放。白俄罗斯还释放了数百名政治犯，其中至少有 148 名政治犯的自由与与美国特使约翰·科尔和特朗普政府的谈判直接相关。 3 月份，在同一外交努力中，又有 250 名囚犯被赦免。
特朗普在中国领导人九月份访问华盛顿时向习近平提出了这些人的案件，支持者原本预计特朗普会在深圳再次这样做。特朗普在五月份访问北京时也曾敦促习近平释放陈。
中国当局于 2025 年 5 月 1 日指控陈从事间谍活动。他的妻子荣友芳表示，陈已因他的研究受到审问超过 100 次，她担心他会因捏造的罪名受审。
陈的工作由美国政府资助，公开且从未被保密。
“我知道特朗普总统已经就解决又林案向习主席提出了两次要求，我希望中国政府能够在特朗普总统12月在佛罗里达州接待习主席之前做到这一点，”容周四告诉路透社。
据美国国务院称，敏津应中国政府邀请参加一个学术会议，于 6 月 3 日前往中国云南，随后被捕。路透社
